_doc: Plain-language scoreboard for the C10 problem (made-up multi-word names), shown by tools/dashboard_report.py. The program session updates it at every result and close-out: add a results row, refresh current/queue, rewrite the brief in plain words. Scores are held-out reworded questions answered exactly right, out of 72. Full detail lives in CORPUS; this file only points there.
brief: We are trying to teach the model made-up names (like a project codename) so it can recall them when a question is worded differently. Ordinary facts already work (about 69 of 72). Made-up two-word names do not: the usual method gets about 9 to 14 of 72. Our best write method so far gives each made-up name its own new word in the model's vocabulary and reaches about 40 of 72; the goal is 61. The 'ceiling' test trains the model directly on the facts. That is not a usable write method; it only shows what is reachable. On its first try it got 70 of 72, against 9 for the usual method in the same run. But it also disturbs nearby facts asked the same way, and part of the success may come from the second word simply following the first. One try does not count, so the repeat run is the one that matters. Where things stand tonight: the repeat run started at 21:42 and is now using the GPU. It is working through its training rounds one after another and should take up to about 7.5 hours, so by about 05:10 at the latest if nothing has to be redone. One risk: if one of the first two training rounds needs a redo, the time limit stops the run and the program will ask you. We have asked whether you will allow up to 9 hours 20 minutes (560 minutes) for that case; you have not answered yet. Before that, the first run of step 4 (letting each fact pick its own depth) finished cleanly at 21:33. Its pre-set rule says no repeat is needed, but we have not called it a result yet: two reviewers look at it first. ASTRA is still being built. Steps 6 and 7 wait for the repeat run.
